newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae net July mortgage portfolio up 12.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae net July mortgage portfolio up 12.3 pct.

text.p: The Federal National Mortgage Association's net mortgage portfolio grew by an annualized 12.3 percent, or $3.0 billion, in July after expanding by an annualized 1.8 percent in June, according to Fannie Mae.
Commitments to purchase mortgages increased to $6.9 billion last month, up from $6.1 billion in June, suggesting further strong portfolio growth in coming months, the agency reported.
The increased commitments in both months far exceeded the $4.5 billion monthly commitment average in January through May.
The net portfolio stood at $299.8 billion in July, after the 12.3 percent annualized jump from the prior month.
Jayne Shontell, senior vice president of investor relations for Fannie Mae, attributed the two consecutive strong purchase commitment months to "a return to more normal spreads in the marketplace."
The spreads she was referring to were between mortgage and debt financing. Fannie Mae buys mortgages for its portfolio and funds them with various debt.

"What we do is grow the portfolio very opportunistically," she said. "When we get the returns that we want, then we do more purchasing. When spreads are narrower, we either don't purchase or purchase very little."

Fannie Mae expects to have double-digit growth for the year, in keeping with the pace in recent years. That would mean a consistent double-digit expansion in the second half, following "somewhat slower growth in the first half of the year," Shontell said.
Fannie Mae reported that the net interest margin on its mortgage portfolio rose one basis point to 130 basis points in July.
The net interst margin is the spread between the yield on the portfolio assets and the funding costs for the entire portfolio of debt and equity.
The total corporate net interest margin, a more liquid portfolio of shorter-term assets and labilities combined with the mortgage portfolio, had an unchanged spread of 116 basis points in July.
Total MBS outstanding increased by $3.3 billion in July to $677.2 billion, a 5.8 percent annual growth rate compared with a 6.1 percent rate in June, Fannie Mae said.

The conventional multi-family at-risk serious delinquency rate fell to an all-time low of 0.47 percent in June, from 0.56 percent in May. For single-family serious delinquencies, the rate edged up 0.58 percent from 0.57 percent.
"Anything really below 1.0 percent is considered excellent credit performance," said Shontell, who forecast a continuation of that trend for the immediate term.
